  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea B is a clearly defined product with a specific user and problem. Idea A's own source marks it 'one-line description to confirm' with customer 'varies by idea', so there is nothing concrete to build or sell yet.",
    "B's demand evidence is broader. It cites independent sources (HN, Reddit, LinkedIn) across multiple years describing the same recurring pain. One poster puts a dollar cost on it (~$43k/year in engineer wait time).",
    "B includes a direct willingness-to-pay signal: 'Solve this and I would pay for it' (HN). A has no comparable buyer statement.",
    "A's demand evidence is self-undermining. The same thread cited as demand contains a rebuttal that vibe coding removes the need for an 'ideas guy'. That points to a shrinking core need.",
    "A's competitors show no real traction: dummy-data teams, illustrative fake profiles, 30 beta testers. Its only price anchor (CoFoundersLab, $29/mo) is an adjacent category and carries a billing class-action caveat.",
    "B has a defined zero-cash acquisition path (HN/Reddit/dev.to posts) that existing competitors have demonstrably used, plus a priced paid option (daily.dev ~$380/issue). A's channel cost estimate comes from an unverified vendor blog.",
    "B's competitors already shipped working MVPs as solo hobbyists. That confirms one person with AI agents can build a credible product within 90 days, leaving time to test a paid tier."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence rests on a single Reddit thread viewed through a mirror site. The quote is a vague 'looking for someone to make apps with', and the same thread directly rebuts the premise ('there is no such thing as an ideas guy anymore'). That is one ambiguous post, not evidence of a paying need.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B wins clearly on problem definition and demand quality, but its own brief shows serious risk to a paying customer within 90 days. Roughly seven free open-source competitors exist, no paid comparable exists in the category, and individual developers are hard to convert from free tools. Getting a first payer for B likely depends on finding a team or hosted feature the free tools lack. A, by contrast, is too undefined to evaluate properly."
}
